quest.title: Please, great shaman!
quest.description: After you sincerely beseech her, Citlali finally agrees to help. But to your surprise, Granny Itztli's name does not merely bring with it assistance...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x425, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

chapter.num: Memories Flowing With Color: Act III
chapter.title: The Truth of the Battle of Seven Colors

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You don't seem super invested in this whole thing, Citlali...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The Battle of Seven Colors is something I've only ever heard about. I know as much as anyone else in my tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But how? Weren't you alive when it happened?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I wasn't there when it took place, and she never told me about it — that's how.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, Montluson said the two of you were close friends. The battle was legendary! Why wouldn't Huitzilin tell you about it?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Close friends? More like archrivals — something Montluson would know if he actually did his research.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Did you see the graffiti outside my house? That's not my doing.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: All students from Huitzilin's school of shamanism must pass an extremely difficult trial before graduation — defeating me in battle.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Those graffiti drawings are how they challenge me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait, what?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Of course, none of them ever succeeded.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: So, after Huitzilin's death, her students had no choice but to modify the requirement. Instead of defeating me, all they have to do now is last long enough.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, that sounds like a necessary change...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: As my rival, Huitzilin only had one achievement that surpassed my own, and that was the Battle of Seven Colors. I can only assume she had some kind of secret technique at her disposal.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It makes perfect sense that she kept it from me. I'm a fast learner — telling me about the technique is no different than handing it to me on a silver platter. As if she would give away her one advantage...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, that makes sense.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Anyway, all of that is secondary. Like I said, I'm only here to help you fulfill your duty.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So, Citlali is doing all this... for me?)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: D—Don't misunderstand... This duty is important for my tribe, too. A great shaman should do her part to see it done.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (A great shaman should also be bit more... organized at home.)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Excuse you, I fail to see what housekeeping has to do with my duty as a shaman...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Why is it that you're the one whose thoughts are exposed, but I'm still the one suffering...? I need to get to the bottom of this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pfff...

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Excuse me, great shaman, but we have a situation over here. We could really use your help!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Please, great shaman!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Okay, okay...

dialogues.speaker: Atihk
dialogues.text: Of course the Battle of Seven Colors happened! The woven scroll proves it! Huitzilin used a mysterious color to construct a maze and trap the enemies inside!

dialogues.speaker: Badru
dialogues.text: That's just your interpretation. There's more than one way to understand that scroll. Besides, constructing a maze out of a color? It's ridiculous!

dialogues.speaker: Atihk
dialogues.text: Huitzilin was one of the most powerful shamans of her time. She definitely could have pulled it off!

dialogues.speaker: Badru
dialogues.text: That's the biggest problem! She had students — why not pass it down?

dialogues.speaker: Badru
dialogues.text: A technique that powerful, and no shaman since has ever used it?

dialogues.speaker: Atihk
dialogues.text: Her students are keeping it a secret, of course! If you knew a technique like that, you'd be a fool to show it to just anyone!

dialogues.speaker: Badru
dialogues.text: Hmph!

dialogues.speaker: Atihk
dialogues.text: Hmph!

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: I didn't mean to cause an argument. I just wanted to ask... Is there anything we can use to prove the battle took place?

dialogues.speaker: Atihk
dialogues.text: Of course it took place! Why would you need to prove it?

dialogues.speaker: Badru
dialogues.text: You'll have to excuse him. Some people in our tribe insist on clinging to outdated views of history. I'd give up now if I were you — it only gets more ridiculous from here.

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: Please don't fight...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, so the battle really is controversial...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Am I the outdated one? Kids these days can't find anything better to argue about?

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: These arguments are precisely why I hesitate to include this story in my collection.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Neither side was able to offer anything useful... What should we do?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Huitzilin was a passionate teacher... We were opposites in that sense. The technique she used in the battle must have been her masterpiece. There's every reason to pass it on.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Still, if the technique is powerful enough to single-handedly stop an invasion, it also makes sense that her disciples would keep it a secret.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: We should check with the students from her school. If we can confirm the technique exists, we can deduce certain things about the battle.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: But, as far as I know, most of the shamans from her school occupy high positions in the tribe — not the type of people outsiders like us can speak to on a whim...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ah, right, the Obsidian Altar is off limits to you. But, uh, if I go...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is there a problem?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Most of Huitzilin's students are respected priests in the tribe. But, that means they had to go through me... or try, at least. I, of course, humiliated them from a young age.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Those who hold the position now are the ones who lasted long enough before I wiped the floor with them.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: If I show up without warning, they'll run for dear life... That's not gonna get us any answers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, Paimon can see it now...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Run for dear life? It's like Citlali's some kind of tyrant...)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hey, don't jump to conclusions! That was just a metaphor!

choices.text: I'll make sure they don't run away.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: #Heh, only you have the guts to joke like that with me, {NICKNAME}... Fine. I said I'd help, so I'll help. But, don't blame me if it goes wrong.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright! The rest of you can wait for us here!

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: We appreciate the help!

choices.text: Who better to fend off a "tyrant" than a hero of Natlan?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Oh, are you in the middle of a ceremony?

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Granny Itztli!?

dialogues.speaker: Aywastin
dialogues.text: Wh—What is she doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Besuci
dialogues.text: Did some coward not show up after challenging her to a fight?

dialogues.speaker: Chogan
dialogues.text: Or... is she here to officially take over the tribe?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, it's like they really do see her as some kind of tyrant.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: No matter what, we'll defend our dignity as priests to the end!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You talk a big game for someone who lost to me the most out of the entire priesthood.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: All I want is to ask some questions...

dialogues.speaker: Aywastin
dialogues.text: So, you're here to... interrogate us?

dialogues.speaker: Besuci
dialogues.text: Someone didn't sit pretty for their beating, is that it? You want their name, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Chogan
dialogues.text: We should just run!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't be afraid.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! With the hero of Natlan here, Granny Itztli will be on her... best behavior!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Sure, whatever you say.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: #Oh, it's {NICKNAME} and {M#his}{F#her} companion... That does make me feel better. How can we help you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We wanted to ask about the technique you inherited from Huitzilin...

dialogues.speaker: Aywastin
dialogues.text: Heh, so you can eradicate our school once and for all?

dialogues.speaker: Besuci
dialogues.text: Disciples of our school have challenged her year after year, just as our master instructed. Sounds like she's finally had enough...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Well, you're not wrong...

dialogues.speaker: Chogan
dialogues.text: If we want to protect our legacy, one of us needs to run!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not this again... Just how much did you traumatize them, Citlali?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (She beat them in a duel. So what? There's no reason to be this terrified. Citlali is someone worthy of love and respect.)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hey! You can't just... say whatever you want just because it's in your head.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'm Granny Itztli — a mere mention of my name, and kids burst into tears. Love and respect? Heh, no one has the guts for that.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Well, I do.)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Wh— You know what, forget about your duty. We really need to fix this mind-reading situation!

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Sorry to disappoint, but if you're here to question whether we're qualified to inherit our master's legacy, we... we're not going down without a fight!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #We're not getting anywhere... What should we do, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let me think...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh, it's you...

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Elder Tlapo... We must have disturbed your meditation. Our deepest apologies. Please, forgive us.

dialogues.speaker: Aywastin
dialogues.text: Did... Did Elder Tlapo just issue a declaration?

dialogues.speaker: Besuci
dialogues.text: From what I can tell... In a single word, the message was "friend"?

dialogues.speaker: Chogan
dialogues.text: Is Elder Tlapo telling us to... treat Granny Itztli as a friend?

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: ...That's not possible, is it?

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Oh, you forget yourselves, my friends. You are esteemed priests of our tribe. Where are your manners?

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Chief...

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: I didn't expect to see you here, Great Shaman. My sincere apologies for the lack of hospitality.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...Well, I wasn't exactly planning to come to this crowded place, so you can save the pleasantries, Chief. I'd rather get this over with.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Understood... Now, as successors of Huitzilin, I understand your friction with Granny Itztli.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: However, Elder Tlapo's declarations have always showed us the correct path. You would do well to respect his counsel.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: So, mind your manners and allow Granny Itztli to ask her questions.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew... Good thing Elder Tlapo and Chief Biram are on our side.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi there, Elder Tlapo!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, he seems pretty happy to see us!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: He's the one who put you in charge of the scroll, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, Elder Tlapo appointed us to the task!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Elder Tlapo, huh... He's still "Claw" to me.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hey, don't pull that cutesy stuff with me. You're an Iktomisaur Elder now. You occupy an eminent and important position within the tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, you already know each other?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Claw was only this big when we first met. He was Huitzilin's saurian companion back then. She kept dragging him to my place, so, over time, we got to know each other.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like you and Huitzilin were close.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: She only came to my place to fight me. But, at the same time, she always claimed to be my friend. She was the only one who dared to try, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Well, you've lived a long time! You've probably made a bunch of friends over the years, right?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The more time you have... the more friends you lose.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, um...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Anyway, let's get back to business. I hate talking about the past.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Two hundred years, and you still haven't given up, Claw?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #I still haven't made up my mind, so you should head back... {NICKNAME}, Paimon — let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, Chief Biram!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hello, Biram.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, wait, we haven't reached out since the last time we failed the task, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Haha, I'm just grateful you haven't forgotten that duty.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, we have good news! We found another clue.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: I'm all ears.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's the Battle of Seven Colors!

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Huitzilin's claim to fame? That sounds promising... But, the battle took place hundreds of years ago. An investigation is bound to be difficult.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: True, but Granny Itztli promised to help!

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Is that so? I've tried seeking her help in the past, but I never managed to coax her out. You should cherish this opportunity.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hey, don't complain — none of the previous chiefs succeeded, either.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Ah, forgive me — that wasn't my intention. It was a comment on my own failings.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Paimon said you've been trying to figure out how to weave the special scroll?

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: It is my duty, great shaman.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Why bother? The scrolls always end up completed on time, so what's the point of figuring it out for yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: If I may, this task concerns the history of Natlan as a whole, and in many ways, history is the memory of a people.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Memory is sacred to our tribe. I'm sure a great shaman understands that better than a humble junior like myself. Something this important cannot be left to baseless rumors.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: I know you don't concern yourself with the daily affairs of the tribe, Granny Itztli. Even so, as a priestess, I trust you wouldn't leave something like that to chance.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I get your point...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Something on your mind, Citlali?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Of course, the one time I wish you could read my mind, it doesn't work...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The chief referred to himself as a "humble junior." Maybe Citlali's worried she looks old?)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: No, that's not it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #It's not important... Rest assured, Biram, with my help, {NICKNAME} and Paimon will definitely be able to complete the task.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: You have my thanks, then.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: So, are you here to test whether we're qualified to inherit Master Huitzilin's legacy?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You've already been tested, haven't you? Frankly speaking, I don't think any of you are qualified.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But, that's not why I'm here. All you need to do is be good and answer my questions.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Fine... Ask away.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You've heard of the Battle of Seven Colors, right?

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Of course! It's our master's claim to fame, an immortal legend inscribed in the very history of our tribe!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Then, I'm sure you know there are those who question whether it actually occurred.

dialogues.speaker: Aywastin
dialogues.text: I did hear people arguing about that the other day...

dialogues.speaker: Besuci
dialogues.text: It's disgraceful! How can they question something like that?

dialogues.speaker: Chogan
dialogues.text: It doesn't surprise me. Natlan has had more tourism lately. A lot of people have started getting strange ideas after interacting with outlanders.

dialogues.speaker: Chogan
dialogues.text: After all, everyone who took part in the battle has returned to the Ley Lines. Without witnesses, it's hard to refute detractors.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Well, it just so happens... the questions I want to ask are directly related to the legitimacy of this battle.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Listen... We know you were rivals, but do you really have to question her legacy?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You think she's like you — someone who can't survive a little scrutiny?

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: No, of course not!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Then, let me finish. During the battle, Huitzilin most likely used a technique powerful enough to turn the tides of war. I'm sure she was very proud of it.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Proud enough to pass it on to her disciples. So, which one of you inherited that technique?

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Uh... I don't think any of us have heard of it.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Listen, I'm not trying to take it for myself, so be honest! With or without it, I can wipe the floor with any of you.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Yeah, no objections there... But, I'm telling the truth! None of us have ever heard of that technique.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Tch, what's wrong with her? Why would she let it go extinct?

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Master's body of work is massive. No one student could hope to learn all her techniques... Mastering just a few already takes a lot of effort.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Master had no choice but to recruit many students, split up what she knew into different portions, and pass it down through various individuals.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: So, even though we see ourselves as representatives of Huitzilin's school of shamanism, what we know isn't the sum of her legacy.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Actually, I know of a shaman family that inherited some of master's techniques. The family fell on hard times and lost the right to the priesthood. Still, could be worth a shot...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, if they inherited Huitzilin's secret technique, shouldn't the family be thriving?

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Well, it's the only thing I can think of...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...Alright. Give me their address.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: I'll mark it out on your map.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: To be honest, I'm not optimistic about the future of this investigation.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're really giving it your all, though.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: That's because the request came from you. You don't know the power of your own words, do you?

talks.objective: Meet up with Montluson and the others

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You recount everything you learned to Montluson and the others.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Proving the legitimacy of this battle seems more hopeless by the second.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Nothing we can do about that.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: ...Well, even if our investigation ultimately proves the legend to be false, that's still a worthwhile result.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Although I'm here for business purposes, I have a personal interest in this as well. I'm drawn to matters of historical truth.

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: That's exactly why I chose to follow you, Monsieur Montluson!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Listen, I'm just updating you on the situation, not asking for your opinion. I don't really care whether you continue your investigation.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Um...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, you came to me for help with your scroll-weaving duty, right?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You thought looking into the Battle of Seven Colors could give you answers — that's understandable. But, based on our progress, I'd say this is a dead-end.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Instead of wasting time, you might consider taking a different approach. I'll try to think of another way to help you.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: #Respected {NICKNAME}, let's not forget about the compensation I promised! You shall have it in full — extra, if that's what it takes!

choices.text: I think this investigation...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: What makes you say that?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Because it has to do with Huitzilin's past.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, based on what you've told us so far, it kinda seems like there's unresolved tension between you two.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Y—You... think so?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She claimed to be your friend, but picked fights with you nonstop... and never told you about her biggest accomplishment.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: By figuring out the truth behind the battle, maybe we can finally help you get closure!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Closure? I'd say we're two hundred years too late... But, fine. If you want to keep investigating, be my guest.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: Ah, that's wonderful news!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, let's go visit the shaman family!

choices.text: Could help you, too, Citlali.

talks.objective: Find a member from the shaman family

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: Sorry, I just wanted to ask... Is Granny Itztli satisfied with my answer?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, of course! You really helped us out!

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: Oh, good. I'm glad I didn't offend her somehow...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're really that scared of her?

choices.text: She's actually really nice.

response.speaker: Etchemin
response.text: To be honest, Granny Itztli almost never interacts with ordinary tribespeople like us. Everything we know about her comes from rumors.

response.speaker: Etchemin
response.text: She's a powerful shaman who's lived for over two hundred years. As a great hero, you're probably the only one who isn't intimidated by her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, thanks for today, Citlali!

choices.text: Wanna grab a meal? My treat!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hm, that's quite considerate of you. Alright, let's grab a few drinks, just like last time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, didn't you say you had "important plans" tonight...?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: What did you think I meant?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Does that mean you've gone drinking every night for the past two hundred years? Now, Paimon's worried about your health...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Same place?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: No, I've had enough socializing for one day... I know somewhere quiet. We can just buy some drinks and head over.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Which will also give us a chance to solve the mind-reading issue. Considering the necessary spell work, I'd rather do it in private.

choices.text: Think of it a thank you for today.
She's just... awkward in social situations.

talks.objective: Board the hot air balloon with Citlali

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Citlali leads you to a hot-air balloon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, this is like a secret base!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Sometimes, I want the fresh air, but not the company, so I come here.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Let's see if my stash is still here... Great, the Halberd-Crest Birds didn't eat my snacks.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...Now for the mind-reading issue. Give me your hand.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just like last time?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It might take a little longer, actually. I just need to share my senses, make a clean break...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: And... that should do it, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This really is a one-of-a-kind view. That must be why Citlali likes to come here.)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You're not wrong... Hold on! Why do I still hear you in my head?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No idea...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Did I not separate our senses completely? Maybe using my palm isn't enough... Close your eyes!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (Please work! Please work! A great shaman should be able to handle this...)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Okay, what about now?

choices.text: I think I heard something...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Huh!? And now?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's gone.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Huh, whenever I try to remove the effect, it just flips direction and gets worse...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Was that Citlali's forehead just now? It was really warm...)

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: That was just to help with the spell... Shoot, I still hear you...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: ...For a human soul, to lose the boundaries of the mind is to drown in the sea of consciousness without a concept of self...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, that sounds bad!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I read that in a light novel. When it comes to the real world, I think it's pretty accurate...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, is Citlali drunk? She's not making much sense...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Anyway, we'll just have to leave it for now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hearing {NICKNAME}'s thoughts isn't that bad, right? You should just tease {M#him}{F#her}! That's what Paimon would do.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: It's just... I'm not good at this. I'm not used to being close to people.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Sorry, I said we could be friends, but I guess I'm not ready.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I'm used to being Granny Itztli — someone intimidating, someone people are scared to approach. I don't have to deal with people that way.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why live like that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, Paimon's been wondering... Why do you insist on living so far away? You could easily become a leader of your tribe, someone everyone loves and respects...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: When you live as long as me, a person is like a flower.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: The color draws you in. You water it to see it bloom. It rewards you with its fragrance...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: But, it doesn't last. With the passing of the seasons, everything withers away. You can try to water it, but it will never bloom again.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Even if the same plot of soil is covered in flowers the following year, the one you remember won't be there.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: That's just how it is — most of the people in my life will be gone one day, just like a flower.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Getting close means losing friend after friend for hundreds of years... until the weight of their memories crushes my soul.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: If people don't care about me, then I don't have to care about them. It's better if the people in my memories are nothing more than fleeting strangers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Citlali...

choices.text: My approach is different.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: You won't live as long as me, so you don't have to worry about that.

choices.text: Actually, I might have a long lifespan...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Really?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Then, you should understand.... Nearly everyone you know will be gone one day.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: All the more reason to remember them.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: #{NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I have a friend who only lives in my memories now. In fact, you could say my memories are the sole proof that she existed in this world.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (So, sometimes I tell myself... As long as I remember every single friend, they will never truly die.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Instead, they will live on in the world of my memories.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (When friends create memories together, there's always something to hold on to. So, if you still need time, let me choose to remember you first.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is something wrong?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Stupid mind-reading side-effect won't go away... It's not like I want to hear you complain about me all the time...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, she's definitely drunk... Uh, Citlali? Maybe take it easy. At this rate, you might sleep past noon tomorrow...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: #I'm not drunk... I remember everything {NICKNAME} said.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Just gotta... think of a response... I'll think... of something...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh oh, not this again... Is she asleep?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I... I'm fine... can... get home... by myself...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is she talking in her sleep or talking to us? She seems kind of out of it...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Bye... Gonna walk back... alone... Need some time... to think...

choices.text: She doesn't need us to worry about her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright...

choices.text: She's always been like this.
I have some truly ancient memories...
I choose to remember everyone.
It sounded like your thoughts...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello! Are you Etchemin?

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: Yep, that's me... Huh? Granny Itztli!?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Get up... In a crowded market like this, the only person who should be trying to hide is me.

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: M—My apologies... Ever since my grandfather's generation, the shamans of my family have given up on passing your trial, Granny Itztli. Have we... offended you in some other capacity?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Man, this is generational trauma at this point...

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: Whenever I misbehaved as a kid, Grandpa would tell me about the thrashing he received from Granny Itztli. I still get nightmares about it sometimes...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I wonder what Citlali looks like in those nightmares...)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hey, don't get any funny ideas! This was your idea, remember? Keep asking your questions. I'm going to find somewhere quiet to wait.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, so, your family studied under Huitzilin, right?

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: Yes, although that pretty much ended with my grandfather's generation, unfortunately.

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: The techniques my family learned from Huitzilin didn't have much practical use in terms of tribal affairs, so during my grandfather's time, we quit the priesthood.

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: Turns out, shaman techniques aren't that useful outside the priesthood, either. So, over time, we abandoned them altogether...

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: Of course, it's possible that we were just too foolish to understand the true power of those teachings...

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: After all, Huitzilin was a genius. None of her students have been able to fully reproduce her talent.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you know which techniques were passed on to your family?

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: I'm not sure... As a kid, I remember hearing my grandfather talk about them, but it's not like I can use them myself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just think about it for a sec... Do you remember anything about a technique that can decide the outcome of a battle?

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: Decide the outcome of a battle? No, I don't remember anything like that.

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: Besides, my family wasn't really known for our talent. If a technique like that exists, I doubt Huitzilin would pass it on to us.

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: You might have better luck asking one of the priests. They're descendants of Huitzilin's most gifted students.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, looks like we're back where we started.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Still no definitive evidence the Battle of Seven Colors took place... Allier, do you think we have enough to draw a conclusion?

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: All we have are non-witness accounts. We could put together an interview, but that's not going to hold up in academic circles.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Then, we have to keep going...

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: Oh, you're investigating the Battle of Seven Colors?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! You know about it?

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: Not a lot, but there's something special about my family — in addition to shaman techniques, Huitzilin's stories were passed down to us as well.

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: Say what you want about my ancestors' dedication to shamanism, but they definitely paid attention to those stories.

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: And of course, the Battle of Seven Colors is the most exciting story of them all.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: We don't need another story, we need something concrete! Does no one in your tribe understand that?

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: I'm not sure if this is helpful, but the story passed down in my family is a little different from the one told in the tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How so?

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: Well, it's Huitzilin's personal account of the events, so it's a lot more detailed.

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: For example, in the version I heard, the battle took place in a location known as "Chicomostoc Cave."

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: That means you can tell us where to find it! Have you ever been to this place?

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: Unfortunately not...

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: I studied maps of Natlan before we left, Monsieur Montluson. I don't remember ever seeing such a name...

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Hmm... Could your ancestors be mistaken, Mr. Etchemin?

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: It's unlikely. My family may have let the shamanism side of things fall by the wayside, but we're serious about these stories.

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: In the words of my grandfather... Some things deserve to be passed down more than secret arts.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: If Huitzilin's version of events differs so much from the general understanding, that makes it even more likely the battle is completely made-up...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah... That's disappointing.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hold on, you mentioned Chicomostoc Cave?

dialogues.speaker: Etchemin
dialogues.text: Oh, um, yes. Can I... clear something up for you?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It's been more than two hundred years... I never thought I'd hear that name again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: That location is now known as The Valley of Fog. Chicomostoc Cave is what it was called two hundred years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: Precisely when Huitzilin was alive! That means... Monsieur Montluson, we can confirm the original site of the battle!

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: Once we get there, the evidence we need should be at our fingertips...

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Haha... Just when we thought all hope was lost! I never doubted you, Great Shaman. Allow me to present you with a gift as thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Save it... Flattery won't get you anywhere with me.

choices.text: Just accept the gift, Citlali.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, Mr. Montluson works in publishing! You're a huge fan of light novels, right Citlali? Maybe he could get you some that are out of print?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: R—Really?

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: Out of print, huh... Sure! Do you have any in mind?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Well, if we're talking collectibles, then the first edition of "Shogun Almighty: Reborn as Raiden With Unlimited Power" is a must.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: It's the first major hit of the isekai genre. Several editions have gone to print, but copies of the first edition are exceedingly rare and valuable.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: I see...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: There's also its sister work, "Pretty Please, Kitsune Guuji?". It was Yae Publishing House's attempt at gauging the new market trends.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: It opened the door to a new genre after readers grew tired of isekais. The sales speak for themselves.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Actually, Yae Publishing House released a limited edition not too long ago, but it's almost impossible to get. Anyway... I'll take those two.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: Sorry, I'm not sure I caught all that... What were the titles again? Reborn as... Kitsune Guuji?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hah! These two titles are among the most successful and well-known works in the entire industry. You're telling me, as someone who works in publishing, you've never heard of them?

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: ...I'm a merchant from Fontaine, after all. Regarding this particular genre from Inazuma, I'm afraid I lack your level of expertise.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hah... Amateur.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: Um...

choices.text: Just leave the books to me.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: Of course — sounds like a perfect arrangement! Now, there's no time to waste. We should head to the site of the battle right away.

response.speaker: Allier
response.text: Once we get there, it'll take a bit more work to determine the actual location. Right now, all we have is a general idea.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: Well, I'm sure Miss Citlali can help us with that!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Have you even looked at the time? It's already evening, and I have important plans tonight. You expect me to work through the night?

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: #Um, well... What do you think, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: Let's break for the day and meet back up tomorrow.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: Okay, we'll find a place to rest for the night. When should we meet tomorrow?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He's persistent, huh...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What do you think, Citlali?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hmm... How about noon?

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: Do we have to wait that long?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Great shamans have important matters to attend to in the morning.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (My guess is that she just wants to sleep in...)

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Th—That's only because I have important tasks to complete at night!

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: Alright, as Miss Citlali instructed... Let's meet back up tomorrow at noon. We'll be waiting at the exit of the tribal settlement.

choices.text: The battlefield's not going anywhere.
Don't forget about our pay, though.
You've earned it.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Miss Citlali seems rather... reluctant to help. Maybe you could talk to her a bit more. I'll reward you for the trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: Natlan's history is full of intriguing mysteries. It's too bad I can't talk to those priests myself...

dialogues.speaker: Grudoc
dialogues.text: Got a problem? Like I said, take it up with my employer.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Why does Granny Itztli want to question us all of a sudden?

dialogues.speaker: Aywastin
dialogues.text: Should we plan our answers in advance?

dialogues.speaker: Besuci
dialogues.text: That brutal "graduation exam"... It's all coming back to me...

dialogues.speaker: Chogan
dialogues.text: You heard the Chief... There's no running away.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: If you run into any more problems, I'm always willing to help.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: I hope Granny Itztli's satisfied with the information we provided...

dialogues.speaker: Aywastin
dialogues.text: So... was that an interrogation?

dialogues.speaker: Besuci
dialogues.text: That poor coward... I should go find him and convince him to accept his fate.

dialogues.speaker: Chogan
dialogues.text: Ah... You scared me. I was just about to run some errands. If you have questions, feel free to ask the other priests.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this the place?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: No, further up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Further... up?
